title: Scanner page -- non-blocking pr-reviewer follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of frontend-market-scanner-page's PR #243, tracked here so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: Add a Playwright e2e spec under frontend/tests/e2e/ for the /scanner page (frontend-market-scanner-page): at minimum the golden path (category picker -> run scan -> results table -> add to watchlist) plus the disabled/unavailable state, matching the pattern of the existing dashboard/portfolio/watchlist specs. The persisted e2e suite currently has no coverage of the Scanner page at all -- only pr-reviewer's own one-off Playwright walkthrough exercised it.

Round 3 review nit: ScannerResultsTable.tsx's `ErrorOutlineIcon` is imported from `@mui/icons-material/ErrorOutlined`, not `ErrorOutline`/`ErrorOutlineOutlined`. `ErrorOutlined` is the 'Outlined theme' variant of MUI's `Error` icon (its SVG path is byte-identical to `Error.js`'s) -- a filled solid-circle error icon, not the lighter hollow-circle `ErrorOutline` family the variable name implies. Purely cosmetic (still clearly reads as an error) -- swap the import to `ErrorOutlineOutlined` (or rename the local alias to match `Error` if the solid icon was actually intended) so the name and the rendered icon agree.

Round 3 review nit: ScannerResultsTable.tsx's retry `IconButton` sets `disabled={addWatchlistItem.isPending}` inside the `if (addWatchlistItem.isError)` branch, but this is dead code -- TanStack Query's mutation reducer resets `error`/`isError` to `null`/`false` in the same synchronous dispatch that sets `isPending: true` (`@tanstack/query-core`'s `mutation.ts`, the `'pending'` case), so `isError` and `isPending` can never both be true and this branch is never actually rendered with `disabled` true. Harmless (clicking retry while a previous retry is still in flight just calls `mutate()` again, which TanStack Query already handles safely), but remove the dead prop or, if the intent was genuinely to disable the icon while a retry is in flight, use a separate local 'retrying' flag instead of relying on `isPending` inside the `isError` branch. RESOLVED as a side effect of round 5's redesign (PR #243): the separate `<IconButton>` this dead prop lived on no longer exists at all -- ScannerAddToWatchlistButton now renders one persistent `<Button>` with no `disabled` prop anywhere in any state -- so there is nothing left to clean up here. Marked done by pr-reviewer's round-5 re-review rather than left stale.

Round 4 review (non-blocking design note, distinct from that same round's blocking focus-loss-on-retry-success finding): ScannerAddToWatchlistButton's failure announcement uses `role="status"` (implicit `aria-live="polite"`) rather than `role="alert"` (implicit `aria-live="assertive"`). The round-4 fix's own `decisions` entry says this was chosen specifically so it wouldn't reintroduce the `queryByRole('alert')` landmark ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx's round-3 regression test asserts is gone -- but that test was written to confirm the *full ErrorState block* (an icon+heading+body element large enough to break row layout) was removed, not to forbid role="alert" on any element whatsoever; a visually-hidden live region with `role="alert"` would have zero layout impact and wouldn't reintroduce the layout regression the test actually guards against. WAI-ARIA authoring practice generally recommends `role="alert"` (assertive) specifically for action-failure announcements like this one, since a polite region can be skipped or queued behind other speech if AT is already announcing something else, whereas the alert role interrupts. Worth reconsidering as role="alert" (relaxing/rewriting the existing `queryByRole('alert')` test to target the ErrorState-block absence more precisely, e.g. asserting on a heading/testid rather than the alert role itself) the next time this component is touched.

Round 4 review (non-blocking, from a parallel code-review pass): common/UnavailableState.tsx's `message` prop is only rendered under a plain truthy check (`{message && (...)}`), so a backend `detail` of `''` (an empty string is a valid value for the `string | null` schema type, distinct from `null`) silently renders no message line at all -- both ScannerPage and ScannerPanel pass `message={data.detail ?? 'fallback text'}`, and since `''` is not `null`/`undefined` the `??` fallback never applies either, so the result is a bare heading with no explanation. Narrow (requires the backend/gateway to actually return an empty-but-present `detail` string, which isn't currently observed from any code path) but easy to close either by having `UnavailableState` treat a blank string the same as absent (e.g. `message?.trim() && (...)`) or by having the two callers coalesce an empty string to the fallback themselves (`data.detail || 'fallback text'` instead of `??`).

Round 5 review, non-blocking (from a parallel code-review pass on PR #243's round-5 commit cc077bf): `ScannerAddToWatchlistButton`'s redesign correctly never applies the native `disabled` attribute in the pending/error states (doing so would blur a focused element, reintroducing the exact focus-loss bug this redesign eliminates) -- but it also dropped `disabled={added}` for the terminal, already-succeeded `added` state, which was never part of that bug (a settled 'Added' button isn't mid-transition, so disabling it doesn't blur anything -- there's no pending/error state left to swap back from). The 'Added' button is now clickable forever: clicking it again calls `handleAdd()` -> `addWatchlistItem.mutate(...)` again, firing a redundant `POST /api/watchlist` and, on its `onSuccess`, `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: watchlistKeys.all })` -- a real refetch and a visible icon flicker (Check -> CircularProgress -> Check) for an action the UI already told the user is done. Not a correctness bug (`POST /api/watchlist` is an idempotent no-op on a ticker already watched, per API.md, and this was independently confirmed live: a real click-again in a Playwright/Chromium session against a mocked backend produced exactly one extra successful POST, no error, no duplicate row) and no existing test asserts non-interactivity of the 'Added' button either way. Fix without touching the native `disabled` attribute at all (which is what caused this to be dropped in the first place) -- e.g. a JS-level guard at the top of `handleAdd` (`if (added) return`) rather than a `disabled` prop -- that would preserve the redesign's whole rationale (no natively-disabled focused node, ever) while removing the redundant network round-trip and flicker.

Round 5 review, non-blocking nit: `frontend/src/features/watchlist/hooks/useAddWatchlistItem.ts`'s new exported function signature (`export function useAddWatchlistItem({ mutationKey = watchlistKeys.add }: UseAddWatchlistItemOptions = {}) {`) is 107 characters, exceeding this repo's configured Prettier `printWidth: 90` -- confirmed with `npx prettier --check src/features/watchlist/hooks/useAddWatchlistItem.ts` from `frontend/`, which reports the file as unformatted. Not caught by this project's enforced static-analysis gate (`static-verify`'s `yarn lint`/`tsc -b` steps don't run `prettier --check`), so non-blocking, but worth wrapping across multiple lines (or running `yarn format`) the next time this file is touched.

decisions.decision: The new frontend/tests/e2e/scanner.spec.ts's golden-path test stubs GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params and POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run at the browser's own network boundary via Playwright's page.route(), rather than driving the real, unmocked backend the way every other spec in this suite does. POST /api/watchlist (the add-to-watchlist half of the flow) is left unmocked, hitting the real running e2e backend and database, with a test.afterAll DELETE cleanup mirroring watchlist.spec.ts's own pattern for GOOGL. The mocked scan result uses a synthetic symbol ('SCANE2E') distinct from every real fixture ticker (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA/GOOGL) the other four spec files already claim.
decisions.rationale: playwright.config.ts's webServer never sets FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED, so GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params always reports state: 'disabled' in this e2e stack (app/config.py's ibkr_enabled defaults to False) -- there is no environment (sandboxed, CI, or dev container) with a live, interactively-logged-in IBKR gateway to enable it against (app/data/ibkr_provider.py's own module docstring makes the same point about its pytest suite). Driving the real backend unmocked, as every other spec does, can therefore never reach the 'available' state the golden path needs to exist at all -- there is no way to test the real category-picker/run/results/add flow against a genuine gateway response in this pipeline, full stop. Two alternatives were considered and rejected: (1) skip the golden path entirely and only cover the disabled state -- rejected because the task explicitly asks for the golden path 'at minimum', and the disabled state alone leaves the actual pick-a-category/run/results/add-to-watchlist flow (the bulk of this feature, and everywhere ScannerResultsTable/ScannerCategoryPicker/ScannerAddToWatchlistButton's real behavior lives) with zero persisted e2e coverage; (2) stand up a stub HTTP server implementing IBKR's Client Portal Web API endpoints as a third playwright.config.ts webServer entry, with FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED=true and FINTRADE_IBKR_BASE_URL pointed at it -- rejected as materially larger scope than this follow-up task (a new, ongoing-maintenance-cost stub gateway implementation) for a benefit page-level route interception already delivers: proving the real frontend renders/wires the real backend's actual state-shaped response correctly end to end. Route interception is one layer further out than IBKRProvider's own pytest suite's HTTP-boundary mock (the browser's fetch boundary vs. the httpx.Client boundary), but is the same substitution for the identical underlying constraint, not a new category of test-double this codebase hasn't already accepted elsewhere for this exact reason.

decisions.decision: Added `data-testid="error-state"` to common/ErrorState.tsx's root element, and rewrote ScannerResultsTable.test.tsx's 'not the full ErrorState block' assertion to `queryByTestId('error-state')` instead of `queryByRole('alert')`, as part of switching ScannerAddToWatchlistButton's failure-announcement live region from role="status" to role="alert" (this task's checklist item on that role).
decisions.rationale: Once the per-row live region itself uses role="alert" (always mounted, per-row, even when empty), `queryByRole('alert')` can no longer distinguish 'no full ErrorState block rendered' (what the round-3 regression test was actually built to guard) from 'the row's own now-always-present live region exists but is empty' -- the two rows in that test's fixture data mean `queryByRole('alert')` would in fact throw (multiple matches) rather than silently pass, catching this immediately. The checklist item's own suggested fix named 'a heading/testid' as the alternative; ErrorState has no unique heading (its heading text varies per HTTP status, and per-status text already has its own passing assertions in ErrorState.test.tsx), so a stable data-testid on the block's own root -- matching the existing data-testid convention already used by WatchlistTable/FundamentalDataPanel/HomeworkScoreBanner and others in this codebase -- was the more precise, status-code-independent choice over asserting on any specific heading string.

review.notes: Full review of PR #302: checked out task/frontend-market-scanner-page-followups, ran backend pytest+coverage (1244 passed, 100% line/branch coverage) and frontend vitest+coverage (882 passed, 99.7%+ statements/branches), ran static-verify (backend ruff+mypy clean, frontend eslint+tsc clean, profit-target wording guard clean), `npx prettier --check` on every touched file (clean; the repo-wide check flags 85 pre-existing unrelated files, none touched by this PR), and `scripts/validate_tasks.py` (clean). Ran `make e2e` twice (26/26 passed both times, including the two new scanner.spec.ts specs) to check for flakiness -- none observed; also ran the touched vitest files three times in isolation with identical results. Manually traced: (1) the new e2e spec's page.route() stubbing of GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params and POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run against the real ScannerPage/ScannerPanel component tree and confirmed the aria labels/roles used in the spec (heading 'Scanner', combobox 'Scan category', table 'Scanner results') match the actual rendered markup; (2) the role="status"->"alert" switch plus new data-testid="error-state" on common/ErrorState -- confirmed no other test in the touched files or elsewhere in the suite queries getByTestId('error-state') (so no cross-test collision), and that the per-row always-mounted role="alert" Box in ScannerAddToWatchlistButton is a structurally distinct element from ErrorState's own role="alert"+data-testid="error-state" root (the two never coexist in the same render branch), and confirmed ScannerPanel.test.tsx's own queryByRole('alert') absence assertion only fires in the gateway_unreachable branch where ScannerResultsTable (and its per-row alert boxes) is never rendered at all, so the role switch didn't break that assertion; (3) UnavailableState's message?.trim() change against its two call sites (ScannerPage/ScannerPanel) and its new blank/whitespace-string tests; (4) the terminal 'Added' button's `if (added) return` guard via the new regression test, which counts actual POST /api/watchlist calls (not just button label) and confirms exactly one POST fires despite three clicks. Backend was untouched by this PR (frontend-only diff) -- no OpenAPI/API route changes, so no snapshot regeneration was needed. No new module/component/layer was added (only existing common/ and feature components edited), so architecture-review and the common/-vs-feature placement check (step 7a) don't apply here. Independently ran the code-review skill (high effort) in parallel, which reached the same conclusion (zero findings) after its own separate verification pass (icon import path exists, role="alert" usage traced across the whole test suite, backend watchlist route assumptions confirmed). No blocking or non-blocking findings from either pass.
